Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran a quick internal sizing exercise and want to start with dedicated capacity commitments that map to our Q4 launch plan. High-level ask below:

- US: sustained 80 concurrent inference streams, avg seq 512, peak token rate ~1.2M tokens/hr
- EU: sustained 40 concurrent streams, avg seq 400, peak token rate ~600k tokens/hr

Can Redwood provide a recommended tranching/packing plan and a timeline for provisioning if we commit to a 6-month reserved contract? Also please highlight any networking/KMS compliance needs for APAC.

Marissa / team — quick feasibility notes:

- Baseline: to support 120 concurrent @ seq 640 reliably under our latency SLOs wed recommend an APAC dedicated pool with 48x H100-similar cards (dense config) OR 96x A10G-equivalents depending on model quantization. H100 path reduces network serialization and KV cache pressure.
- Lead time: we have two options:
  * Soft-burst (preferred short lead): schedule capacity on our cloud partners as burst instances (72-96h provisioning) — higher unit cost but fastest.
  * Dedicated pool (recommended for cost/runbook): ~3-5 weeks to allocate and configure in SG given current procurement and compliance slots.
- KMS/HSM: we can integrate with customer-managed KMS in SG but will need SOC2 evidence and a signed DPA amendment before we enable customer-provided keys.

I attached a short SOW draft and the network compliance checklist for Galileo to review.

Attachments: SOW-draft-Galileo-v1.docx (SOW stub), network-compliance-checklist.pdf

Next steps I need from sales: confirmed commitment window (6 vs 12 months), whether they accept soft-burst pricing for first 8 weeks, and a contact for KMS onboarding.

—Olga
Director, Infrastructure Planning
